purpose: Close Junyo/Hiyo/Ryujo/Zuiho hull location, air-group attachment, deck readiness and 11/26 rear-support reach without importing Bengal combat deployment or later-1944 maturity.
precedence: Historical movement only as fallback when no Branch causal chain contradicts it
hard_guards: Centered Bengal carrier hull commitment is zero.
No Bengal combat fatigue is charged to Junyo/Hiyo/Ryujo/Zuiho.
Historical Junyo 1943-11-05 HALIBUT torpedo damage is not inherited on the centered line because the Ultra-cued interception chain is broken.
Hull location, air-group location, deck readiness and aircraft count are separate clocks.
Secondary carriers are not equivalent to Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu/Soryu fast first-line decks.
Kinsei Zero is not assigned to these secondary decks as a default pre-GALVANIC fighter type; late Zuisei remains the main fighter pending event-specific trial/allocation.

mobilization_trigger.centered_order: 1943-11-14..15 Pacific-priority release of secondary carrier reserve after the large US amphibious signature becomes credible
mobilization_trigger.interpretation: This is not foreknowledge of Tarawa. It is a response to a large Central-Pacific amphibious operation signature.

branch_path: Survives Branch divergence and remains a secondary/light carrier.
Historical fallback Yokosuka departure 16 Nov / Truk arrival 21 Nov has no identified Branch contradiction.
Zuiho.position_1943_11_23T00: Truk lagoon / Combined Fleet rear-deck concentration
Zuiho.air_group_position: aboard / Truk-linked; no separate southern combat deployment
Zuiho.deck_state: OPERATIONAL; low-to-moderate transit fatigue; refueled/replenishing but usable

branch_path: Participates in May Attu limited-relief force and is released afterward.
Spends summer/autumn as mobile reserve/ferry-patrol-training asset; no Bengal combat charge.
Historical 31 Oct Truk-to-home movement is usable as a fallback.
Historical 5 Nov HALIBUT torpedo damage is removed on centered Branch line; Junyo therefore reaches home waters serviceable instead of entering battle-damage repair.
Pacific-priority order around 14-15 Nov permits an eastbound redeployment from Inland Sea/Saeki around 15-16 Nov.
Junyo.air_group_position: aboard/reconstituted with ship; no historical Solomons emergency-rebuild location automatically inherited
Junyo.deck_state: OPERATIONAL; routine-maintenance and transit fatigue only

branch_path: Survives Branch divergence and participates in May Attu limited-relief force.
Released after Attu and not permanently tied to the Aleutians.
No historical TROM is usable after 1942; autumn position must be constructed from Branch mission policy.
Centered autumn duty is home/central-Pacific reserve, ferry, patrol and deck-training rather than Bengal combat.

Because Ryujo is the most useful small forward deck for search/CAP/ferry under the Branch mission-class doctrine, October US carrier pressure gives a positive reason to keep her in the home-to-Truk rotation rather than west of Singapore.
Ryujo.position_1943_11_23T00: Truk lagoon / immediate vicinity; centered arrival 19-21 Nov after Pacific-priority release
Ryujo.deck_state: OPERATIONAL; small-deck limitations remain; Branch deck-processing improvement applies only to suitable wind/load
Ryujo.sensitivity: If autumn rotation left Ryujo in home waters as late as 15 Nov, arrival can slip to 21-23 Nov; this changes 11/23 immediate CAP/search by roughly one light-deck wallet but not 11/26 availability.

branch_path: Available after earlier repair/workup; Branch does not copy Solomons emergency attrition/rebuild state wholesale.

Historical fallback has Hiyo still in Inland Sea and departing south only on 25 Nov with Ryuho; that southbound ferry/transport movement is not realized once Branch Pacific-priority is issued around 14-15 Nov.
Centered Branch response advances departure to about 17-18 Nov for Truk rather than waiting for the historical 25 Nov southbound movement.
Hiyo.position_1943_11_23T00: Inbound to Truk, roughly final 0.5-1.0 day of transit; centered Truk arrival during 23 Nov
Hiyo.deck_state: TRANSIT-OPERATIONAL at T00; becomes full rear-deck operational after arrival, refuel and handling reset later 23-24 Nov
Hiyo.11_23_immediate_use: NOT_FOR_EARLY_DAWN_GILBERT_MARSHALL_COMBAT; available after Truk arrival for local/rear tasks

aggregate.rule: These are combat-usable aircraft across heterogeneous rear decks, not one synchronized strike package. CAP/search/recovery/ferry reservations reduce any offensive follow-on sortie substantially.

geometry.home_to_Truk: about five days-class at operational transit speed, weather/escort dependent
geometry.Truk_to_Eniwetok_rear_area: about two-to-three days-class at operational transit speed
geometry.consequence: A carrier at Truk by 23 Nov can plausibly enter rear-support geometry by 25-26 Nov without becoming part of the first-line four-carrier strike core.

operational_closure.11_23: Junyo/Ryujo/Zuiho may already relieve local/rear CAP/search and prepare eastward movement. Hiyo is not credited to the dawn 23 Nov tactical wallet.
operational_closure.11_24_25: All four can be refueled/reorganized and move east in staggered rear echelons if Yamamoto keeps the carrier-commitment gate open.
operational_closure.11_26: All four are available as rear-deck shock absorbers/CAP-search-recovery support; they are not automatically added to the first-line 160-class strike. A limited second strike must be separately generated from remaining aircraft, fuel, escort, distance and deck cycle.

reopened_dependencies: Exact escort/DD hulls assigned to eastward carrier transit must be paid when surface-force OOB is closed.
Per-ship aircraft role mix must be closed after the 11/23 Marshall/Nauru local-air OOB so airframes are not double allocated.
Whether Ryujo is placed one echelon farther east than Junyo/Hiyo is an operational deployment decision, not a location fact at 11/23T00.
